overall_quality.evidence: Processes and threads are both fundamental concepts in operating systems, but they serve different purposes and have distinct characteristics. Processes are the basic units of execution in an operating system, each with its own memory space and resources. Threads, on the other hand, are lightweight components within a process that share the same memory space and resources. They are used to improve the efficiency of a process by allowing multiple threads to run concurrently within the same process. Threads are more efficient for tasks that require frequent context switching, such as I/O operations, and can be created and destroyed more quickly than processes.
